note.after_visit_summary: You have moderate to severe psoriasis that has worsened over the past few months, affecting your elbows, knees, lower back, and scalp. Creams and methotrexate haven’t controlled it well, so we’re starting a biologic medication called risankizumab. It’s an injection given under the skin every 12 weeks after two starter doses. Before starting, you need blood tests for TB, hepatitis, blood count, and metabolic panel—these can be done at the lab at 2250 Riverside Drive. We’ll also seek insurance approval using your member ID K as in kilo 7 0 3 9 2 1 5. In the meantime, continue using clobetasol ointment on body plaques twice daily but only for two weeks at a time, then take a week off to prevent skin thinning. For your scalp, use clobetasol 0.05% solution once daily at night. Keep taking your amlodipine 5 mg each morning for blood pressure. Avoid live vaccines while on risankizumab, but get your annual flu shot. Watch for joint pain, swelling, or morning stiffness—call us right away if these occur, as psoriasis can affect joints. We’ll follow up in six weeks after labs and insurance approval. Call 555 -0134 with questions.
